answer.says: Shri Hegde, I must be blunt. The confusion of our names is a clerical error, but the consequence is that I occupy a dwelling that does not belong to me, while you, the rightful holder, are left without a roof. I cannot continue to rest in a house where the bread is not bought because I have no money, nor can I ask Ramesh to cook for a master who will not pay him. I am a philosopher, not a thief. I ask you to look at the file again. The state is the ethical idea, but only if it distributes its rights with clarity. Do not let my name be a typo in your ledger; let it be a lesson in the failure of administration. Ramesh, please, bring us tea. I will pay you for the cup, but I cannot pay for the meal I cannot afford. We are all suspended in this haze, waiting for the next order.
answer.thought: The evening presses in, and the hunger is a physical argument that my poverty makes. I look at Hegde, who is the man I am supposed to be, and I see the absurdity of a system that mistakes identity for substance. I must speak plainly; the dialectic of my situation is that I am free in my words but bound by my lack of money. I will not retreat into silence.
